problem:
The vector $v$ in the plane is mapped to the vector $[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2\end{aligned}]$ under the action of the linear transformation $T$ whose matrix $T$ is given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 3 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

What is the original vector $v?$

examples.knowledge_point: Calculating a Vector Given Its Image Under a Linear Transformation
examples.problem:
The vector $\mathbf{v}$ in the plane is mapped to the vector $[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4\end{aligned}]$ under the action of the linear transformation $\mathbf{T}$ whose matrix $T$ is given by
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14062093/assets/371521f0acd44811e109c10460e0cc99eb41d256f37f209dcefc003fd78ea70e.png)
What is the original vector $\mathbf{v}?$
examples.worked_solution:
From the given information, we have

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14062093/assets/c95b308a6f55de3acc8a2bf446b38ac10500dd506795898b0892952147d5c9e7.png)

We need to reverse the action of the matrix $T.$ So, we multiply the above equation by $T^{-1},$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{-1}\cdot T\cdot v & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\ v & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we need to calculate the inverse of $T$, which is

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{-15-(-20)}[\begin{aligned}-3 & 2 \\ -10 & 5\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}-3 & 2 \\ -10 & 5\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the original vector is

$$
\begin{aligned}v & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}-3 & 2 \\ -10 & 5\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 10\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
